name: FortiWeb — IDOR Sequential ID Enumeration
description: Detects Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) / object enumeration against the banking web applications: a single external source (data.original_src) requesting 20+ distinct numeric identifiers (e.g. account numbers) on the same endpoint within 30 minutes. Legitimate corporate-banking sessions access only a handful of accounts (observed max ~8 over 6h), so high-cardinality identifier access from one source indicates authorization-bypass enumeration. Enriched with success vs forbidden/not-found counts for triage.
false_positives: Internal admin tools that legitimately page through resource IDs
Search-engine crawlers with sitemaps containing many ID paths —
query:
FROM logs-tcp.generic-default
| WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 30 minutes AND data.type == "traffic" AND data.original_src IS NOT NULL AND data.http_url IS NOT NULL AND data.http_url RLIKE ".*=[0-9][0-9][0-9]+.*"
| EVAL endpoint = MV_FIRST(SPLIT(data.http_url, "?")), rc = TO_INTEGER(data.http_retcode)
| WHERE NOT endpoint RLIKE ".*rb_.*"
| STATS distinct_ids = COUNT_DISTINCT(data.http_url), attempts = COUNT(*), success = SUM(CASE(rc < 400, 1, 0)), forbidden = SUM(CASE(rc == 401 OR rc == 403 OR rc == 404, 1, 0)) BY data.original_src, data.http_host, endpoint
| WHERE distinct_ids >= 20
| SORT distinct_ids DESC
| KEEP data.original_src, data.http_host, endpoint, distinct_ids, attempts, success, forbidden
| LIMIT 100
